answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. In effect, the network makes cheating the most expensive strategy available, which is the closest thing to a Sybil-resistant design that economics allows.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a mesa as the anchor of the cost.
